q: The first step in posting a journal entry to the ledger is to:

options.A: Open the account debited in the journal and write the account credited in the particulars
options.B: Balance the account on the date of posting
options.C: Strike off the ledger folio number in the journal
options.D: Enter the amount in the Journal column of the ledger

q: In the ledger, the abbreviation L.F. in the journal stands for:
The L.F. column in the ledger contains:

options.C: The folio number of the journal from which the entry was posted

q: In the particulars column of a ledger debit entry, the account credited is prefixed with:
In the particulars column of a ledger credit entry, the account debited is prefixed with:
An account in the ledger is balanced when:

options.A: The balance is transferred to the journal
options.B: Both sides are totalled and the difference is entered to make them equal
options.D: All entries are posted on the debit side

q: 'Balance c/d' written in a ledger account means:
'Balance b/d' written in a ledger account means:
Balance c/d is entered on the side where:
Balance b/d is entered on the side:

options.B: Opposite to where balance c/d was entered
options.C: The same side where balance c/d was entered

q: If the debit total of an account exceeds its credit total, the account shows a:

options.D: Adverse balance to be written off

q: If the debit and credit totals of an account are exactly equal, the account shows:
A personal account usually shows:

options.A: A debit or credit balance depending on whether the person owes or is owed

q: A real account (asset) normally shows:
A nominal account (expense or income) at year-end is:

options.A: Left with its debit or credit balance permanently
options.C: Closed by transfer to Trading or Profit and Loss Account

q: The cash account is balanced:

options.A: Only when an audit is due
options.B: Weekly with a credit balance allowed
options.D: Daily or as frequently as needed, and it never shows a credit balance

q: The cash account can never show a credit balance because:

options.A: Cash payments cannot exceed cash available
options.B: The cash account has no credit side

q: The drawings account at the end of the year is closed by:
Carriage inward is posted to:

options.A: The Trading Account directly without a ledger account
options.B: The Carriage Inwards Account on the credit side
options.C: The debit side of the Carriage Inwards Account
options.D: The Purchases Account on the credit side

q: Carriage outward is posted to:

options.A: The credit side of the Carriage Outwards Account
options.B: The Sales Account on the debit side
options.D: The debit side of the Carriage Outwards Account

q: Discount allowed on prompt payment is posted to:

options.A: The debit side of the Discount Allowed Account
options.B: The credit side of the Discount Allowed Account

q: Discount received from creditors is posted to:

options.A: The debit side of the Discount Received Account
options.B: The credit side of the Discount Received Account

q: In sectional balancing, the general ledger is balanced by:

options.A: Transferring all balances to one account
options.C: Opening control accounts for total debtors and total creditors

q: After posting all journal entries, the book-keeper should:

options.D: Check that the journal's L.F. column is completed for every entry

q: When posting a compound journal entry to the ledger, the book-keeper:

options.A: Posts each debit and each credit to its respective account
options.B: Combines them into one net entry
options.C: Posts the total to a suspense account

q: The date column in a ledger account shows:

options.A: The date the account is balanced
options.B: The date of the original transaction as in the journal
options.C: The date the trial balance is drawn

q: 'To Balance b/d' appears on the debit side of an account when the previous period ended with a:
'By Balance b/d' appears on the credit side of an account when the previous period ended with a:
A debtor's personal account normally shows a:

options.C: Balance c/d on the debit side

q: A creditor's personal account normally shows a:

options.D: Balance b/d on the debit side

q: Posting the journal entry 'Debit Purchases A/c, Credit Ram A/c' results in the ledger entry in Ram's account:
The total of the debit column of a ledger account is written:

options.D: On the line below the last entry on the debit side

q: A trial balance is prepared from:
Which account is NOT balanced but closed by transfer?
The bank account may show:

options.C: A debit balance or a credit balance (overdraft)

q: In the ledger, 'J.F.' column records:

options.C: The joint folio of two accounts
options.D: The folio number of the journal (book of original entry)

q: The main purpose of writing the L.F. number against a journal entry is to:

options.A: Provide an audit trail and avoid duplicate posting

q: Balances c/d of personal and real accounts appear in the balance sheet as:

options.D: They appear in the trial balance only

q: When a ledger account has only one entry, balancing it requires:

options.C: No totals or c/d — the single amount is itself the balance
options.D: Still writing full totals and c/d

q: If a wrong amount is posted to the ledger from the journal, the correct procedure is to:

options.B: Ignore it if the trial balance agrees
options.C: Erase the figure and overwrite it
options.D: Pass a correcting journal entry and post it

q: The debit balance of the Purchases Account is transferred at year-end to:

options.B: The Balance Sheet as an asset

q: The credit balance of the Sales Account is transferred at year-end to:
Returns inward are posted to:

options.A: The Sales Account on the debit side
options.C: The debit side of the Returns Inward Account
options.D: The credit side of the Returns Inward Account

q: Returns outward are posted to:

options.B: The debit side of the Returns Outward Account
options.C: The Purchases Account on the credit side
options.D: The credit side of the Returns Outward (Purchases Returns) Account

q: Bad debts written off are posted:

options.A: To the credit of the debtor and debit of the Bad Debts Account
options.B: To the debit of the debtor and credit of the Bad Debts Account

q: A loan taken from a bank is recorded in the ledger with a:

options.A: Debit balance in the Bank Loan Account
options.B: Credit balance in the Bank Loan Account
options.D: Balance b/d on the debit side

q: Prepaid expenses at year-end appear as:

options.A: A nominal account closed to P&L
options.B: A liability in the balance sheet
options.C: A debit balance carried down as an asset

q: Outstanding expenses at year-end appear as:

options.D: A credit balance carried down as a liability

q: The Capital Account of a sole trader normally shows a:
Interest on drawings is posted:

options.A: Debit Drawings Account, credit Interest on Drawings Account
options.B: Debit Interest on Drawings Account, credit Drawings/Capital Account
options.C: Debit Cash Account, credit Capital Account
options.D: Debit P&L Account, credit Cash Account

q: In the ledger, amounts are always written:

options.B: In the amount column nearest to the particulars
options.C: In the separate debit or credit amount column on the entry's side

q: Cross-referencing between journal and ledger is done through:

options.D: The L.F. column in the journal and the J.F. column in the ledger

q: An account showing 'To Balance c/d' on its debit side has:
An account showing 'By Balance c/d' on its credit side has:
The balance of the Stock Account at year-end is:

options.C: Carried down as a debit balance and shown as an asset

q: Depreciation for the year is posted:

options.A: Debit Machinery Account, credit Depreciation Account
options.B: Debit Cash Account, credit Depreciation Account
options.D: Credit Machinery Account, debit Depreciation Account

q: The Depreciation Account at year-end is closed by transfer to:

options.C: The Balance Sheet as an asset

q: Posting is usually done:

options.A: Once a year after the trial balance
options.B: Periodically — daily, weekly or monthly — from the books of original entry
options.D: Before the journal entry is written

q: A ledger account that has equal debit and credit totals needs:

options.C: No balance c/d or b/d entry

q: The golden rule applied when posting 'Debit Cash, Credit Capital' to the ledger is reflected as:

options.A: Cash A/c credit 'By Capital A/c'; Capital A/c debit 'To Cash A/c'
options.D: Cash A/c debit 'To Capital A/c'; Capital A/c credit 'By Cash A/c'
